Standard or calendar update periods for MTD: what the choice means, the dates, and when you can change it

By Daniel Wyatt · Facts checked 22 November 2026

Short answer: the choice only changes where each quarter ends. Standard update periods end on the 5th (5 July, 5 October, 5 January, 5 April); calendar update periods end on the month-end (30 June, 30 September, 31 December, 31 March). The deadlines are the same for both: 7 August, 7 November, 7 February and 7 May. GOV.UK links calendar periods to accounts that run 1 April to 31 March. Software defaults to standard, and once you send your first quarterly update for a tax year, the choice is fixed for the rest of that year.

GOV.UK pages, HMRC's developer guide and providers' own help pages read on 22 November 2026, linked under each section. GOV.UK's Send quarterly updates page was last updated on 16 October 2026. HMRC software finder data as captured 18 November 2026.

The dates side by side

Each quarterly update covers the tax year so far, not just the latest three months. GOV.UK's tables:

UpdateStandard update periodCalendar update periodDeadline (both)
16 April to 5 July1 April to 30 June7 August
26 April to 5 October1 April to 30 September7 November
36 April to 5 January1 April to 31 December7 February
46 April to 5 April1 April to 31 March7 May (the following tax year)
  • When you can send. GOV.UK says any time after the end of the update period, up to and including the deadline. You can also send up to 10 days before the period ends if you don't expect any more transactions.
  • Nothing to report. If you had no income or expenses in a period, GOV.UK says you still send the update.
  • More often is allowed. GOV.UK says you can send updates more often, but each must still cover the full period from the start of the tax year.

Source: GOV.UK, Send quarterly updates (Update periods and deadlines; When to send an update; Sending updates more often).

Who GOV.UK says each one is for

Your accounting period (the period your books cover)What GOV.UK saysDigital records start
6 April to 5 April (the tax year)Use standard update periods. Nothing to change in your software.6 April
1 April to 31 MarchUse calendar update periods. GOV.UK says this makes record keeping simpler.1 April
Ends on 1, 2, 3 or 4 AprilEither type leaves your records covering a different period from your accounts. GOV.UK says adjustments are needed so annual totals match your accounting period and the late accounting date rules apply.Not stated separately
Any other date (for example 31 December)GOV.UK says you'll need to make additional adjustments in your software after the end of the 2026 to 2027 tax year, with guidance to follow.Not stated separately

GOV.UK also says that if you have an agent, they can tell you which to use if you're not sure. HMRC's developer guide (written for software makers) says only customers whose accounting period starts on 1 April benefit from calendar periods, and that software should not let other customers make the change. Not every product enforces this: FreeAgent's help page says it won't restrict the choice whatever your accounting dates.

Why 31 March works: HMRC's developer guide says that from 2024 to 2025, accounting periods running 1 April to 31 March are treated as equivalent to 6 April to 5 April, removing small adjustments of a few days. For traders, HMRC's Business Income Manual explains the rule: where accounts end between 31 March and 4 April, profits for the days up to 5 April are treated as nil for that tax year and arise in the next one, unless the trader elects otherwise.

Sources: GOV.UK, Create digital records (When to start creating digital records); GOV.UK, Adjust your self-employment and property income (Adjustments because of your chosen accounting period); HMRC developer guide, Change to calendar quarters; HMRC Business Income Manual BIM81210, Late accounting date rules; FreeAgent help, Switch to calendar quarterly update periods.

When the choice locks, and how it's made

  • Default is standard. GOV.UK says your software will be set to standard update periods, and checking your accounting period is one of the steps before you start creating digital records.
  • Before your first update. Calendar periods have to be selected in your software before you send your first quarterly update. After you send an update, GOV.UK says you can't change your update periods for the rest of that tax year.
  • In software, not HMRC online. HMRC's developer guide says the change can't be made through HMRC online services; it's done through software. It also says someone signing up late in the tax year can still make the change, as long as it's before their first quarterly update.
  • Per business. HMRC's July 2026 agent update tells agents to make the selection for each of a client's self-employment and property businesses.
  • It carries on. HMRC's developer guide says a calendar choice continues year on year until you change back to standard through software.
  • Switch years start differently. HMRC's developer guide says that in a year you change, the first period's start date reflects the type you used before. FreeAgent's help page describes this as a first calendar quarter starting on 6 April if you're switching to calendar, and a last quarter ending on 5 April if you're switching away.

How it looks in two products, from their own help pages:

  • FreeAgent: Taxes, then Income Tax, choose the tax year, "Edit tax year details", then "Calendar year quarters". FreeAgent says the option only appears once the tax year has started (for 2026 to 2027, not until 6 April 2026).
  • Sage 50 Accounts: Connected services, then MTD for Income Tax Settings, where "Update period type" can be set to Calendar or Standard before the first quarterly update. After that, Sage shows a message that the update period can't be changed once a quarterly update has been submitted for the tax year.

Sources: GOV.UK, Send quarterly updates (Changing your update period); GOV.UK, Get your software ready; GOV.UK, Agent update: Making Tax Digital for Income Tax (7 July 2026); HMRC developer guide; FreeAgent help; Sage knowledgebase, Set up your MTD for Income Tax settings.

If the setting doesn't match your accounts

GOV.UK's adjustments page covers the main cases for accounts running 1 April to 31 March:

  • Started in 2026 to 2027 and selected calendar periods: no adjustment of this type after the end of the tax year.
  • Started in 2026 to 2027 and forgot to select calendar periods: adjustments after the end of that tax year, with further guidance to be published later.
  • Tested the service in 2025 to 2026 on calendar periods: income and expenses from 1 to 5 April 2025 are added to the 2025 to 2026 annual totals, because those volunteers' first period started on 6 April. GOV.UK says this isn't needed in later years if you stay on calendar periods.

GOV.UK's worked example for an accounting period ending on 3 April: accounts run 3 April 2026 to 2 April 2027, but calendar periods run 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027, so the 2026 to 2027 annual totals remove 1 and 2 April 2026 and add 1 and 2 April 2027.

Source: GOV.UK, Adjust your self-employment and property income.

Which software lists calendar update periods

GOV.UK's checklist for choosing software includes that it must work with your accounting period (standard tax year, calendar update periods or neither). On HMRC's software finder (our copy taken 18 November 2026), 134 of 179 products list calendar update periods as ready now, so 45 don't. Of the 134, 92 are also listed for the tax return, 36 have a free version and 72 are bridging software for spreadsheets.

Things worth checking in your software

  • Which update period type each business (each self-employment, UK property and foreign property business) is set to before the first update of the tax year.
  • Whether your period type shows in the software's list of obligations or deadlines. GOV.UK says that after you send an update, the recent activity in your HMRC online account says "You sent a quarterly update".
  • If you're changing software during a tax year, which period type your updates have already been sent under, since it can't change until the next tax year. GOV.UK says you can change software at any time, but you may find it easier at the end of the tax year. See also spreadsheets and bridging software.
  • Late quarterly updates can earn penalty points after your first required year. See MTD penalty points explained.

Sources: GOV.UK, Send quarterly updates; GOV.UK, If your circumstances change (If you need to change your software).

What GOV.UK doesn't say

  • How to switch back from calendar to standard periods for a later tax year: GOV.UK's MTD guidance doesn't spell it out. HMRC's developer guide says it's done through software.
  • Where the first calendar period starts for every case: GOV.UK's table shows 1 April, but the text under it gives the third update as covering "6 April to 31 December". HMRC's developer guide explains that the start date depends on the period type you used the year before.
  • The adjustment guidance for people who forgot to select calendar periods in 2026 to 2027, or whose accounts end on other dates: GOV.UK says it will publish this later.

Quick answers

What's the difference between standard and calendar update periods?

Only where each quarter ends. GOV.UK says standard update periods follow the tax year (6 April to 5 April), so quarters end on 5 July, 5 October, 5 January and 5 April. Calendar update periods end on 30 June, 30 September, 31 December and 31 March. GOV.UK says the quarterly update deadlines are the same for both: 7 August, 7 November, 7 February and 7 May.

Do calendar update periods give me a different deadline?

No. GOV.UK says 'The deadlines for your quarterly updates are the same for both.' A calendar quarter ends a few days earlier than the standard one, but the deadline stays on the 7th of the following month (7 May for the last quarter of the tax year).

Which update period does GOV.UK say to use?

GOV.UK says to use standard update periods if your accounting period aligns with the tax year (6 April to 5 April), and calendar update periods if your accounting period runs from 1 April to 31 March, because that makes record keeping simpler. It adds that if you have an agent, they can tell you which to use if you're not sure.

What happens if I do nothing?

Your software uses standard update periods. GOV.UK says software defaults to standard periods and that calendar periods have to be selected in the software before your first quarterly update.

Can I change my update period after sending an update?

Not for the rest of that tax year. GOV.UK says you cannot change your update periods for the rest of the tax year after you send a quarterly update. HMRC's developer guide says a calendar choice carries on year after year until you change back to standard, and that the change is made through software, not HMRC online services.

I forgot to pick calendar periods and my accounts run to 31 March. What now?

GOV.UK says that if you started in 2026 to 2027 and forgot to select calendar update periods, you'll need to make adjustments after the end of that tax year, and that further guidance will be published later.

My accounts end on another date, like 31 December. Can I use calendar periods?

GOV.UK only describes calendar periods for accounting periods running 1 April to 31 March. HMRC's developer guide says only those customers benefit and that software should not let others make the change. For other accounting dates, GOV.UK says you'll need to make additional adjustments in your software after the end of the 2026 to 2027 tax year, with guidance to follow.

Does all MTD software support calendar update periods?

No. On HMRC's software finder (our copy taken 18 November 2026), 134 of 179 products list calendar update periods as ready now. GOV.UK says the software you choose needs to work with your accounting period.
